verdicts.why: ديري بالِك (feminine command to Amal) is a valid form and Amal's reply only names دير بالك as the command form in answer to his example attempt, with no rejection of his words.
غيم is a valid collective for clouds (Amal later accepts it at 38:43-38:47), and her 'one?' prompt is a clarifying question, not a correction of a wrong form.
Amal answered 'Mm-hmm. واحدة. Great job.' and her chat just says wa7de, so she took the answer (the feminine واحدة was the target) and gave no signal of a word-order problem.
Her own chat spells it tallajat, so the engine's تلجات is just the she-past تلّجت (she had already said ممتاز to تلجت at 35:27) and her vowelled recast is cleanup, not a fix.
'The wind came a lot' did not mean strong; Amal asked what it meant twice and gave 'it was very strong' in English, after which he said كان قوي كتير (a voiced vocab fix).

He is repeating her own sentence النار حرقتني from 6 seconds earlier and asking if it counts; the engine's English 'me' is a transcription artefact and it falls under the repeat-of-her-correction rule.
He asked 'is it رمل?' as a guess and sand under the ground is not wrong (her own chat later lists ramel among the things in the ground); her رملة sand is a gloss, not a correction.
He said mish fi hon (engine fused it to فيهن); Amal gave an explicit 'مش في' is wrong, 'مش هون', and explained في means 'there is', and her chat confirms مش هون.
